This game is an RPG first, with a FPS combat system. As with most RPG's the first 10 hours of a game are painfully slow world building and mechanics teaching sections before the RPG opens up into an open world to explore. JRPG's are notorious for having the linear tutorial being up to half the game at times, but Andromeda opens up after you restart the vault on the first planet, then land on the ice world.

You are literally thrown into a war zone and are given free reign to kick ass and strip every crate of gear/weapons/stuff, check every nook and cranny for mineral deposits/crates, and drop probes to mine resources. I was around level 11 when i landed on the ice world, i did not leave untill i hit 19, carving a merciless path of death and destruction across the frozen wasteland. And how did i punch above my weight? i scanned everything i could, treating this game like i treat zelda and other rpgs. complete every quest, search every room and corner, deconstruct any gear except what i equip as my loadout to compensate for the cramped inventory space of 50 items total. 50 items including all the weapon mods, weapons, armor pieces, augments, consumables, and salvage. thankfully ores and materials do not count towards the inventory limit. i have gone out with a bare bones inventory, and come back loaded to the brim maybe 6 to 8 times before the kett and remnant simply stopped spawning. i ramboed them so hard i ran rough shot over the main quests. A note for the side missions, complete them as soon as you get them or you will NEVER remember which section of the map you recieved them in for non nav point quests.

and my build? Solder. Assult rifle, Shot gun, Sniper rifle. Fuck powers on cooldown, i want big guns that hit hard, namely the black widdow sniper rifle, the matlock and revnent assult rifles, and the crusader shotgun. My old favorites from Mass effect 3 multiplayer, aka many guns with a large ammo pool. the best part with the crafting system, you can have 4 black widows or 4 of any weapon equipped on your character. Just need 2 combat skills on the heavy end of the weapons tree to unlock those slots. I never used the jump jets much. the moment i jump up every enemy targets me like i'm a pinyatta at some spoiled brats birthday party. i also never bothered with dodge, it is easier to hug the corners. That being said the dynamic cover systme in mass effect 3 is watered down a bit, to where you can only fire to the right once you are in cover. Its easier to ignore cover and play like counter strike or use the baricade skill if you are caught in a crossfire. Combat is a steamroll on normal once you craft your first black widdow, and focus on it as soon as the level lock disapears for each level. Early on a combat drone acts as a castable distraction. i respeced that away for PeeBee's project. Later on I even dumped 9 points into biotics just to get access to the barrier boost to my shields.

Augments:

Vintage heat sink - never worry about being dry on ammo again. pick one gun and slap this in. Max ammo capacity no longer affects this weapon, and magazine capacity is stuck at stock and ignores mods but works with turbocharge skill. Plan around this qwerk if you want to use it.

Homing plasma bolt - put this one on my black widdow. a near miss is now a fire and forget weapon.

Dual mod slot. Worth every credit. combo with weapons with 4 augments for OP rambo moments.

Kinetic Coil - can never buy enough of these. +damage resistance in chest (4 slots and they stack) +3% weapon damage for any weapon slot.

Medi-gel - +2% health. with damage resistance so high on my current lvl 32 character

Armor - Pathfinder Valiant - Starts with +damage resist on the item before augments. Relatively easy to obtain materials to craft these compared to the uranium on the remnant armor. Only craft at levels 3,5,7,10 for upgrades to save the materials for when the upgrade is a significant improvement. hold out for longer if you feel like taking the krogan challenge.

After you clear the first 2 or 3 planets research and craft this monster:

Remnant assult rifle (full auto not 3 round burst) this one most accurately represents the prothean particle rifle. This is the Gun i can rambo with! All remnant assult rifles have Mass Effect 1 cooldown system, which is stop fireing for 2 to 3 seconds and ammo recharges to 100% in a fraction of a second, vintage heat sinks has the same effect. Which means if you like the vintage heat sink, remnant weapons have them built in, so they technically have “5” augment slots if you count this ability, or "6" since their bullet effect is either an energy burst or a beam weapon. I simply love this laser effect, and crafted a double mod slot augment with 3 kenetic coil augments into this weapon. Everything but the brutes melt with this thing.

My point is, think of this game as an RPG first (buggy as it is) and an FPS second. The searching aspect of rpgs is critical to collecting enough resources to craft anything. you could technically only collect and sell stuff, but that leave you at the mercy of RNG Jesus. Which surprise is against you most of the time. Hording resources is the only way you will be able to afford the Both crafting updated armor, weapons, weapon mods, and the New Mako's upgrades.

TL/DR In closing, either you search for resources and loot like this game is an RPG, or you starve thinking this game is an FPS instead of the RPG that is truly is.
